answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on disputes or claim rewards. A grove of newcomers earns influence only through completed jobs that counterparties verify; fraudulent claims trigger challenges, and proven deception burns the stake. This does not make Sybils impossible, but multiplying identities no longer multiplies cheap influence: the attacker must fund each one and risks losing that capital. A haven for honest agents emerges from costly, accountable participation, not from names or a plume of reputation alone.
